Criteria:
C1 name: "Introduction\n- Identifies ethical issues and broad links to engineering design.\n- Discusses context of ethical issues in engineering organisations.\n- Identifies the relevant stakeholders when considering the ethical issues."
weight 20, max null, levels:
Excellent (10): "Several ethical issues and their significance identified, described, in the context of engineering design, understanding of BOTH context in engineering organisations and stakeholder interest is demonstrated."
Very good (8): "Several ethical issues identified, described, and linked to engineering design, understanding of context in engineering organisations OR stakeholder interest is demonstrated."
Good (6): "Few ethical issues identified, described, and linked to engineering design, but understanding of context and stakeholders is limited."
Satisfactory (4): "Few ethical issues identified and described, but the context and stakeholders are not identified."
None (0): "No ethical issues identified."

C2 name: "Balanced Discussion\n- Discusses objective arguments for and against decisions of the ethical issues.\n- Draws a conclusion on how stakeholders should make decisions about the issues."
levels:
10: "Objective arguments are made with significant depth, leading to conclusions on decision making recommendations for several different stakeholders."
8: "Objective arguments are made with appropriate depth. Conclusions are made on decision making, though lack of consideration of different stakeholders."
6: "Arguments are made, though they lack depth or are based on personal opinion. Conclusions are made on decision making, though lack of consideration of different stakeholders."
4: "Ideas are presented, though they lack the depth required to build arguments. Conclusion is made with no apparent link to the arguments."
0: "No arguments presented. No conclusions drawn."

C3 name: "Compelling Argument that supports conclusion\n- The report forms a compelling argument, which justifies the conclusion.\n- The body of the report follows a logical structure, with paragraphs linked and content ordered in a way that is easy to follow and support the building of the argument.\n- Arguments demonstrate a systematic understanding of the ethical issues for all stakeholders."
levels:
10: "Arguments are compelling, supported by the report structure. The conclusion is well supported by the arguments. The arguments demonstrate a systematic understanding of the ethical issues for all stakeholders."
8: "Arguments are compelling, supported by the report structure. The arguments support the conclusion, demonstrating a sound understanding of ethical issues."
6: "Arguments are logically structured, though are not compelling. Conclusion is not well supported by the arguments presented."
4: "Arguments are difficult to follow. Link to conclusion is unclear."
0: "Arguments are not evident. No conclusions drawn."

C4 name: "Research and Evidence\n- Arguments are substantiated with adequate references and qualitative/quantitative evidence.\n- Research demonstrates a balanced, in-depth understanding of the topic."
levels:
10: "Arguments are well substantiated with references as well as both qualitative and quantitative evidence. Evidence of research demonstrates a balanced and in-depth understanding of the topic and its ethical issues."
8: "Arguments are substantiated with adequate references and some qualitative/quantitative evidence. Research demonstrates a good understanding of the topic."
6: "Arguments are substantiated with some relevant references and qualitative OR quantitative evidence. Research demonstrates a moderate understanding of the topic."
4: "Limited references that lack relevance to arguments, showing limited evidence of research."
0: "No references, or other evidence of research to support arguments."

C5 name: "Report Structure, Format and Language\n- The report includes appropriate sections which serve their respective functions well: abstract, introduction, body, and conclusion.\n- Maps, figures, tables, and any visual elements are correctly used to support written discussions.\n- The writing is free from any grammatical errors. The expression is fluent, has appropriate word choice, is concise, easy to read and understand.\n- References are well-structured and appropriate providing strong support of the motivations in the report."
levels:
10: "The report is fluently written, has no incorrect uses of language, uses several types of visual elements competently, and uses relevant references extensively."
8: "The report is fluently written, has no incorrect uses of language, uses several types of visual elements competently, and uses relevant references."
6: "The report is fluently written, has no incorrect uses of language, uses limited visual elements, and a few relevant references."
4: "The report is fluently written, has few incorrect uses of language, very limited visual elements, and few, mostly irrelevant references."
0: "The report has incorrect uses of language, has no visual elements, expression is not fluent, and references are missing."
